player_h2h.rederivation_notes: Own chain (written after reading evidence pack: live_series is empty, rules_samples empty, so the contract is unobserved): outcome = sign of X_A - X_B for a named stat. Stages: (1) participation of both players and the unseen non-participation rule; (2) each marginal (TOI by strength state x rate, PP role, credit share for points, shot share for SOG); (3) pair dependence by pair type (linemates share goals, teammates share script/goalie, opponents share pace but oppose script); (4) exact discrete pmf of D with large tie mass, then tie rule. Required inputs: TOI/PP role/lines, per-player rate, pair-type correlation, stat distribution, lineup news, tie/DNP rule text. The author's chain matches this and adds sensible new inputs (co-credit, IPP, share of team SOG). Differences: author states ties and same-game pairing as facts although nothing is observed; two primary 'inputs' are model outputs.

findings.text: rules_verification NO_LIVE_SERIES and the evidence pack has no h2h series or rules text. Everything about tie handling, DNP, stat set (points/shots/saves) and same-game pairing is assumed. The input list is provisional and must be re-reviewed when a real series lists. The unsourced figure 'around a third of pairs for points' tie is a guess, not data.

The record assumes both players are in the same game ('Participation... both players take part', pair-type correlation stage). The evidence target only says 'player A records more of a stat than player B'; a cross-game or multi-game comparison would remove the dependence stage s3 and the pair-type inputs. Not listed in unresolved.

nhl.pair_difference_distribution is labelled primary new input with pregame_knowable=yes, but it is the model's output (pmf of D), not a data input. It inflates the required-input list; the raw inputs are the marginals plus pair-type correlation.

nhl.game_script_prob and nhl.penalty_rates appear in interactions (INT 1 and INT 3) but are neither in existing_inputs, new_inputs nor input_audit for this archetype. INT 2 (pair_difference_distribution, stat_dist, m.rules_text) is a settlement-rule effect, not an input interaction; INT 3 describes covariance cancellation but is labelled other-nonlinear.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: nhl.ipp_by_state and nhl.sog_share_on_ice cite 'NHL API play-by-play (... on-ice players)'. To my knowledge the NHL API play-by-play events do not carry on-ice skater lists; on-ice state needs a shiftcharts join or HTML reports. hh4 only discloses the PP-unit sourcing, not this.

player_points_goals_assists.rederivation_notes: Own chain from the rules text: N+ ladders on goals/assists/points in one game; settles on stat recorded once the player enters, last fair price if 'active but never enters'; first-goal includes regulation+OT, excludes shootout, separate No Goalscorer; F10G is a team-level half-open [0:00,10:00) window; SEASONPPTS is a regular-season total. Player ladder chain: dress/lineup slot -> TOI by state (PP unit, penalties) -> shot volume x quality x finishing vs goalie -> credit share on team goals (IPP) -> team goal environment (convex multi-point rungs) -> OT/empty-net exposure -> settlement edge cases (scratch vs active, stat revisions). Required: lineup/PP news, TOI by state, ixG/shot rate, IPP/on-ice xGF, goalie, team total, penalties/officials, OT exposure. Author chain matches and adds good inputs (IPP, next-man-up, PP termination). Differences: author conflates 'active' with 'dressed' and demotes scratch risk; two of six series (F10G, SEASONPPTS) lack defined input chains here; no OT exposure input.

findings.text: Settlement over-inference: KXNHLAST text is 'If a player is active but never enters the game, the market settles to the last fair market price'. The record's 'establishes' says 'A skater who dresses but does not play'. The text says nothing about a skater who is not active (healthy scratch, ruled out pre-game) or when a player counts as 'active'. nhl.scratch_void_risk is then demoted to KEEP_CONTEXT ('neither YES nor NO ... not outcome probability'). If scratched players resolve No or void, lineup confirmation timing is first-order for YES probability. CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS is missing from unresolved (pp1-pp4 do not cover it).

Two of six live series have no defined input chain in this archetype. KXNHLF10G (either team scores in first 10:00) relies on nhl.first_goal_hazard, which appears only in one interaction and a data feed and is not defined, audited or in any stage input_ids; no team early-scoring-rate, opening-goalie or early-PP input is specified. KXNHLSEASONPPTS (season player points, e.g. Werenski 110+) cites nhl.career_trajectory and nhl.toi_trend in s5, neither defined/audited here, and no season-points chain exists in the unreg record (goals only). pp2 discloses the misfiling but not that the inputs are absent.

Source of truth is asserted ('Official NHL box score and play-by-play') but no sampled rules text names a feed. Strike set '0.5, 1.5, 2.5' is inferred; only 1.5 (KXNHLAST) and 2.5 (KXNHLGOAL/PTS) were sampled. Whether OT and empty-net goals count for N+ ladders is unstated (pp1 only mentions ANYGOAL).

No OT/3v3 exposure input, although KXNHLFIRSTGOAL text explicitly counts overtime and the SOG record adds nhl.ot_shot_exposure. About a quarter of games reach OT and stars log heavy 3v3 minutes; if N+ ladders count OT it shifts 1+ rungs by a few percent relative.

Inconsistent audit labels: nhl.game_script_prob is KEEP_SECONDARY while its reason says 'first-order input'; nhl.goalie_start 'moves goal probability by only a few percent relative' is an unsourced figure. Stage s3 says goals = shots x quality x finishing but no explicit individual shot-volume input (nhl.shot_rate) is in this record; volume is only implicit in ixG.

player_shots_on_goal.rederivation_notes: Own chain (evidence pack has no live series and no rules text, so contract is unobserved; sibling ladders suggest N+ with fair-price rule): availability/lineup slot -> TOI by strength state incl. PP minutes (penalties, unit share) -> team shot volume vs opponent (shots against, score effects, pace) -> player share of team SOG on ice (role, linemates, D-man point shots) -> attempt-to-SOG conversion (blocks, misses, opponent block rate) -> official scorer counting (arena bias, OT shots, shootout excluded) -> overdispersed count mapped to N+ rungs. Required: TOI by state, PP role, SOG/60 and share, team volume/opponent suppression, block/miss rates, scorer bias, penalties, score script, dispersion. Author chain matches closely, including sensible demotions of zone_start_share and shot_location. Differences: all settlement claims are inferences; a duplicate venue input; an interaction built on rules text.

findings.text: No live series and no rules text (rules_verification NO_LIVE_SERIES). OT counting, shootout exclusion, fair-price rule and ladder strikes are inferred from sibling ladders; the list is provisional. Author discloses this (sg1) but several audit verdicts (e.g. venue demoted to secondary because 'recording bias is smaller ... untested') rest on unobserved settlement.

Duplicate: existing nhl.venue ('Rink effects (shot counting bias), home advantage') and new nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor measure the same arena counting bias. The audit keeps venue as KEEP_SECONDARY without marking DUPLICATE_OF; both stay in feeds and coverage.

INT 6 (nhl.venue, nhl.shot_rate, m.rules_text, multiplicative) is not an interaction: m.rules_text is a text artefact, not a numeric factor. m.rules_text is also used in stage s4 and coverage but is not defined or audited in this record.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: nhl.sog_share_on_ice and nhl.opp_sog_for_rate depend on shot events with on-ice skaters from 'NHL API play-by-play'; the new API play-by-play to my knowledge lacks on-ice lists, requiring shiftcharts joins. sg2 covers boxscore SOG but not the on-ice assumption. Also nhl.shot_share_reallocation estimates a pass-through coefficient from small matched-control samples per team-season with no sample-size caveat.

season_awards_and_stats.rederivation_notes: Own chain from rules text: only KXNHLADAMS has text (coach award, tie pays 1/N rounded down); draft series KXNHLDRAFTTOP/DRAFTPICK are title-only. Jack Adams: candidate pool (coaches in office) -> over/under-performance vs preseason expectation (points pace, turnaround, injuries) -> voter narrative (NHL Broadcasters Association ballots at end of regular season, so playoffs irrelevant) -> finalists -> win probability, tie 1/N. Draft top pick: final standings of non-playoff teams -> lottery draw odds -> pick ownership/protections/swaps -> team selection from prospect consensus; draft year unknown. Required: standings/ratings with uncertainty, preseason projections, coach status/news, voting body and calendar, lottery format, pick inventory, prospect rankings. Author chain matches; the correct IRRELEVANT calls on skater inputs are right for these series. Differences: archetype ownership of player awards, a dangling input, speculative tanking interaction.

findings.text: Archetype mapping: the archetype target is player awards and stat leaders, yet the record audits award_stats, pp_role, ixG, finishing, toi_trend, career_trajectory as IRRELEVANT/WEAK because the only live series are a coach award and draft. The six player-award/stat-title series sit in season_futures, whose record does not define or audit nhl.award_stats or nhl.award_voting_rules (see FUT-1). Result: no archetype owns the player production-projection inputs; a consumer reading this entry would drop them. aw5 notes the label mismatch but not this consequence.

Draft series: KXNHLDRAFTTOP and KXNHLDRAFTPICK have no rules or markets, so stage s4 and three new inputs (lottery odds, pick ownership, prospect consensus) are built on an assumed contract (draft year, pick definition, trades). Disclosed as aw1; lottery format claimed from memory (aw3). Treat as provisional.

nhl.standings_stakes is used in stage s2, category coverage, INT 5 and data feeds but is not in existing_inputs, new_inputs or the audit. The catalog defines it as clinched/eliminated rest-of-stars deployment; INT 5 uses it for deliberate tanking for lottery position, a different, speculative mechanism.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: coach_expectation_delta uses 'MoneyPuck preseason projections (free)' and Elite Prospects/TSN consensus rankings; availability of historical preseason point projections for a multi-season calibration is not checked. Jack Adams voting body, ballot timing and treatment of fired or interim coaches are from memory (aw2). No mapping from the delta feature to a vote-share/win probability among about 30 coaches is specified (award_vote_share_model is player-only and lives in futures).

season_futures.rederivation_notes: Own chain from rules text: KXNHLPLAYOFF (qualify, no secondary text), KXNHLWEST (win the Western Conference Finals), KXNHLRECORDWORST (worst record; league tiebreak then 1/N dead heat), award series KXNHLCALDER/NORRIS/ROSS with sampled text (tie pays 1/N rounded down); Stanley Cup, EAST, HART, VEZINA, RICHARD, FINALSEXACT unseen. Team chain: preseason prior + current xG/goal data with posterior uncertainty and drift -> goalie/injury/trade adjustments -> remaining schedule -> points distribution with loser points -> playoff boundary (3 per division + 2 wild cards, regulation-win tiebreaks) -> bracket path -> best-of-7 with 2-2-1-1-1 home ice -> three series to win a conference. Extremum for worst record. Awards: voted (Hart/Norris/Calder by writers, Vezina by GMs) versus counting leaders (Ross, Richard) via projected production x games, injury hazard, tie rules. Author team chain matches well. Differences: player-award inputs are referenced but not defined here; some textual over-claims.

findings.text: Six player-award/stat-title series (Calder, Norris, Ross, Hart, Vezina, Richard) are in this archetype, but stage s5, the settlement coverage and INT 6 cite nhl.award_stats and nhl.award_voting_rules, which are not in this record's existing_inputs, new_inputs or input_audit (the awards record audits award_stats as IRRELEVANT). Only award_vote_share_model and the tiebreak map are defined. Missing here: player rate/games-played projection (points, goals), defenceman TOI/PP, goalie GSAx/starts share for Vezina, rookie role/pedigree for Calder. Art Ross/Richard are season counting contracts whose chain (games_played_hazard, shot/xG rate) lives only in the unreg record.

Text over-reach: s5 says Art Ross and Richard have 'games-played tiebreaks'; the sampled KXNHLROSS rules say only 'If multiple participants tie for the award ... $1/N'. The record's own tiebreak map says 'fewer games played or more goals for Art Ross'. Whether league tiebreaks apply before 1/N is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS. sf1 calls stat-title wording 'unseen' although KXNHLROSS text was sampled (evidence flags it TITLE_ONLY).

KXNHLWEST 'establishes' says the contract mixes 'two series'; winning the conference final requires winning three series (R1, R2, final). KXNHLRECORDWORST 'establishes' asserts tiebreaks 'favour regulation-win counts' though the text says only league tiebreak procedures (sf4 admits this is unverified). No input models the minimum-of-32 distribution for worst record, and KXNHLFINALSEXACT (exact final score) has no home-ice game-win-probability input; series_context is audited as uninformative in November.
nhl.season_sim_distribution is marked DUPLICATE_OF nhl.ratings yet is still cited as a COVERED input (pace_volume, distribution_variance), in a nonlinearity, INT 3 and a data feed.

award_vote_share_model regresses vote share on 20 seasons of finalists only (a few dozen to ~100 rows per award, selection by finalist status, eras mixed) with 8+ covariates; overfit risk and how voter narrative is handled are not listed as MECHANISM_UNCERTAIN here (only aw4 in awards, for Jack Adams).

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting.rederivation_notes: Own chain from rules text: KXNHLSEASONGOALS/PSEASONGOALS pay if player scores at least N regular-season goals (no minimum-games clause); KXNHLSEASONPTS pays on official team standings points (2 for win, 1 for OT/SO loss), greater_or_equal 95; division winners have no secondary text; KXNHLWSTREAK pays 1/N rounded down on ties. Player goals chain: talent prior (shot volume per game x shooting% shrunk, age curve) -> games-played hazard -> TOI/PP role stability -> goals to date + remaining sum with random rate and games -> league scoring environment -> threshold. Team chain: rating posterior with drift -> remaining schedule -> points incl. loser points -> division maximum with tiebreak (regulation wins first) -> streak as extremum over 32 teams with streakiness. Required: ratings/xG/goalie/injuries, schedule, tiebreak rules, game logs, injury history. Author chain is sound; the problem is scope: team inputs are only cross-referenced, and player season points has no chain.

findings.text: Six of eight live series are team-level, but this archetype's own input list is player-level plus three new team items (loser_point_rate, rating_posterior_uncertainty, win_streak_extremum_dist). nhl.ratings, nhl.injuries_pit, nhl.sos_remaining, nhl.standings_tiebreakers are used in stages s4/s5, category coverage and interactions yet are neither defined nor audited here; xG for/against, goalie quality and pdo are absent. sc5 admits the team mechanism 'sits under futures', so this entry as written cannot be relied on for division, team-points or streak contracts.

Player season points (KXNHLSEASONPTS-type contracts, filed under the game-points archetype) have no chain in this record: contract_types lists 'Season point totals' (team) and 'Player goals', and the player chain is goals only (shot rate x finishing). Assist/IPP, on-ice xGF, PP time share and defenceman usage (a 110-point defenceman) are absent from the season setting; games_played_hazard exists only here. The series should be mapped here with those inputs.

rules_verification is VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT, yet sc1 lists CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS (division tiebreak unstated, streak definition of OT/SO wins unstated) and the VAR asserts shootout goals are excluded from player goals as fact while sc4 labels it SOURCE_UNVERIFIED. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED is the accurate label.

Stage s3 says a 60-goal threshold is a steep function of the mean 'because the sd of a season total is only 7-8 goals'. That is the Poisson sd at about 60 and ignores the random rate and games played the same stage describes; total sd is larger (roughly 9-12), so the S-curve steepness is overstated.

nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist (primary, 'input') is a simulation output, not data. Missing driver: schedule sequence (home stands, back-to-backs, opponent strength along the path) for streaks. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: 'NHL API player status' as a free injury history source; the league publishes no official injury feed, so games_played_hazard covariates beyond games missed come from paid or scraped trackers.
